Playbook.name: Account Creation And Added to Local Group - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: An account was created (4720) and added to a security group within 30 seconds - the rule correlates creation with immediate group membership. Triage question: is this rapid provisioning a backdoor account being set up, or normal automated account provisioning?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Create-then-immediately-elevate is a backdoor-account pattern; the speed and the group targeted determine severity.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: Create + group add
Signal.Details: 4720 followed within 30s by a Security Group Management add for the same member.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the rapid create-and-add is backdoor provisioning or benign automated onboarding.

Step.name: The creation and group-add detail
Step.Purpose: Which account was created and which group it was added to - a privileged group is the escalation case.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("4720","4728","4732","4756") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND (winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" OR winlog.event_data.MemberName LIKE "*$target_user*") | KEEP @timestamp, event.code, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName, winlog.event_data.TargetUserName, winlog.event_data.MemberName | SORT @timestamp ASC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: 4720 then 4732/4728 adding to Administrators/privileged group in seconds = backdoor. Add to a benign functional group during onboarding is normal. Note the actor.

Step.name: Did the new account log on immediately
Step.Purpose: Immediate logon by a just-created, just-elevated account is the backdoor being used.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND event.code IN ("4624","4672") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS logons = COUNT(*), types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType), hosts = VALUES(host.name) BY src | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: A logon by the new account soon after creation, especially from a remote source, confirms an active backdoor - escalate.

Node.Condition: Account created then added to a privileged group in seconds by an unfamiliar actor, especially if it then logs on.
Automated onboarding creating an account and adding it to a benign functional group.
Rapid create-and-add to a non-privileged group by a plausible admin with no ticket.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-CREATEADD-DETAIL, INV-02-CREATEADD-USE to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Disable the account; open IR; review the actor.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A provisioning script mis-adding accounts to a broad group.

SOCAction.Item: Fix the mapping; remove errors; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
